hints: Remember that not all viruses are the same inside. Some store their genes as DNA and others store them as RNA, so ask yourself which bases can appear in both types.
Think carefully about thymine. Is it found in both DNA and RNA, or is it replaced by a different base in RNA?
walkthrough:
**Recall what every virus must contain**

All viruses have nucleic acid surrounded by protein. That nucleic acid can be either DNA or RNA, never both in the same virus.

So for a molecule to be in ALL viruses, it must be found in both DNA and RNA.

**Sort the three bases**

Adenine (2) is found in both DNA and RNA. Cytosine (3) is also found in both DNA and RNA.

Thymine (1) is different. It is found only in DNA. In RNA it is replaced by uracil.

**Pick the combination present in every virus**

Since some viruses have only RNA, they will have no thymine at all. Only adenine and cytosine are guaranteed to be possible in both DNA viruses and RNA viruses.

That gives 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect, because it includes thymine. RNA-only viruses use uracil instead of thymine, so thymine is not in all viruses.
options.B: Incorrect, because it includes thymine but leaves out cytosine. Thymine is missing from RNA viruses, while cytosine is in both.
options.C: Incorrect, because it includes thymine but leaves out adenine. Thymine is DNA only, while adenine is in both DNA and RNA.
options.D: Correct, because adenine and cytosine occur in both DNA and RNA, so both DNA viruses and RNA viruses contain them.
